extracted.intended_audience: research scientists who are authors, reviewers, or editors interacting with eLife (prospective submitters and peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for how eLife selects, reviews, and publishes submitted manuscripts, including desired paper qualities, article-type requirements, and the journal's collaborative review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities of an eLife paper
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our goal at eLife is to publish papers that our reviewers and editors find authoritative, rigorous, insightful, enlightening or just beautiful"; eLife publishes "highly influential research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should exhibit authority, rigor, insight, the capacity to enlighten, or exceptional aesthetic/scientific clarity; influence is valued. These are the primary qualities editors and reviewers use to judge submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types and format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife publishes Research Articles (with no limits to the length or number of figures), Short Reports, Tools and Resources, and Research Advances; also Magazine content (Editorials, Feature Articles, Insights, podcasts, interviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose the appropriate article type and consult the Author Guide and Policies for details and requirements for each submission type. Note: Research Articles have no length/figure limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on working scientists' judgment (no artificial limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife does not artificially limit the number of articles it publishes or have a set acceptance rate; the judgment of the working scientists who serve as editors is used to select papers for peer review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial selection relies on the scientific judgment of active researchers serving as editors rather than quotas or target acceptance rates. eLife explicitly does not support the Impact Factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive and collaborative peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Our goal is to make peer review constructive and collaborative."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial decisions are delivered quickly; working scientists make all editorial decisions. Revision requests are consolidated following an open, internal consultation among reviewers to deliver a single, concise set of the essential revisions — emphasizing collaboration, clarity, and limiting requests to essentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of peer review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-review decisions and author responses for published papers are available for all to read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review outcomes and author responses are made publicly accessible to promote openness and accountability in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of editorial process metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly updated metrics relating to the eLife editorial process are available in the Author Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers can consult the Author Guide for up-to-date metrics about the editorial process (e.g., turnaround times); this supports informed decisions about submission and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to Author Guide and Policies for detailed requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For details and requirements for each type of submission, please consult our Author Guide and Policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page states high-level principles; specific procedural, formatting, ethical, and submission requirements are defined in the Author Guide and Policies and should be followed for compliance.
